author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): give convert-notebooks a pip cache dependency file (#271)
body:
* fix(ci): give convert-notebooks a pip cache dependency file

The Setup Python step used `cache: 'pip'` but the repo had no
requirements.txt/pyproject.toml, so setup-python's cache restore
hard-failed every push to main and every PR:

  No file matched to [**/requirements.txt or **/pyproject.toml]

Add scripts/requirements.txt (jupyter + nbconvert), point
cache-dependency-path at it, and install from it instead of an inline
`pip install` so the cache key tracks the real toolchain.

Also add scripts/requirements.txt to both triggers' path filters and
bring the pull_request trigger to parity with push (it was missing the
workflow-file path), so edits to the toolchain or workflow are validated
without running on unrelated PRs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01LmE97zdTJPkQbiyVMjdi7H

* fix(scripts): stop convert-notebooks exiting 1 on first counted item

Under `set -euo pipefail`, `((count++))` returns exit status 1 when the
pre-increment value is 0 (bash: `(( expr ))` is non-zero-exit when expr
evaluates to 0). The first iteration of each counting loop starts at
count=0, so the script died right after echoing the first notebook —
`--list` and `--dry-run` both exited 1 whenever a notebook existed.

This was latent until the setup-python cache fix let the workflow reach
these steps. Replace all three `((count++))` with the set -e-safe
`count=$((count + 1))`.

Verified locally: `--list` -> lists 5 notebooks, …

body:
* fix(sass): mobile audit — contain author card, restore consent z-order, grow tap targets

Four defects found by driving every key route and interactive component
under phone emulation (320-414px):

- author card: flexbox min-width:auto propagated the widest nowrap
  expertise badge, pushing the page past the viewport on <=340px phones —

  taps from — Reject All / Accept All. The rule now excludes
  .position-fixed so the --zer0-layer-* tokens apply again.
- footer: text links (~19px) and icon-only social links (~16px) now meet
  the WCAG 2.5.8 24px tap-target minimum via block padding and minimum
  boxes; visual design unchanged.
- code copy: buttons grown from ~22px to >=24px tall (32px on coarse
  pointers).

Adds test/visual/mobile-responsive.spec.js (smoke tier, Pixel-class
emulation) guarding all four fixes plus offcanvas/search/settings fit and
tap checks, a dismissCookieConsent fixture, npm run test:mobile, and
before/after evidence under test/visual/evidence/mobile-responsive/.

body:
* feat(feedback): runtime "Improve this page" capture → GitHub issue

Replace the flaky build-time "Copilot Agent" dropdown — which baked the whole
issue body into <a href>s at build time and could not capture runtime logs —
with a robust runtime widget: a global FAB + accessible modal that turn a
reader's report into a well-formed, correctly-labeled GitHub issue.

- Capture: request type (_data/feedback_types.yml) + description + live page
  context + a buffered console/error log (core/console-capture.html), shown in
  a preview before submit.
- Robustness: all data injected via jsonify (kills the three-encoder bug);
  labels mapped to labels that EXIST (the old labels=ai-agent was silently
  dropped, so issues landed unlabeled); URL-length guard with clipboard
  fallback; focus trap + Escape + roving-radio a11y.
- AI layer (optional): posts the capture to the chat proxy's new /api/feedback
  route (Claude Code OAuth) to clarify / vet / prioritize / recommend before
  filing; degrades silently to the base prefill when no proxy is deployed.
- Base layer works token-free on plain GitHub Pages.

Also fixes a latent z-index bug: the dialog now opts out of the .zer0-bg-body
flattening rule (position-fixed) and layers above the cookie banner, so its
controls are never intercepted.

Adds the page-feedback marker label, a page_improvement.yml issue form (no-JS
fallback), a regression spec, and before/after visual evidence. Retires

subject: fix(obsidian): graph reads OBSIDIAN_CONFIG.wikiIndexUrl that js-cdn.html emits (#305)
body:
* fix(obsidian): graph reads OBSIDIAN_CONFIG.wikiIndexUrl that js-cdn.html emits

obsidian-graph.js resolved its index URL only from
window.OBSIDIAN_WIKI_INDEX_URL, a global the theme never sets;
_includes/components/js-cdn.html emits the baseurl-aware value as
window.OBSIDIAN_CONFIG.wikiIndexUrl instead. The graph therefore always
fell back to a <base>-relative path, which 404s on project sites with a
non-root baseurl.

Read OBSIDIAN_CONFIG.wikiIndexUrl first, keeping the legacy global as a
per-page override and the <base>-relative path as the final fallback —
the same chain obsidian-wiki-links.js already uses.

Fixes #294

author: Amr
subject: ci(release): make release-please bump Gemfile.lock and package-lock.json with version.rb (#312)
body:
Every release PR red-failed CI at the 'Version <-> Gemfile.lock consistency'
gate because release-please bumped lib/jekyll-theme-zer0/version.rb without
touching Gemfile.lock. release-please's ruby strategy ships a built-in
GemfileLock updater, but it is a silent no-op unless 'component' is set
(gemName falls back to '' and the updater returns content unchanged).

- set component: jekyll-theme-zer0 so the ruby strategy rewrites the
  'jekyll-theme-zer0 (x.y.z)' PATH spec line in Gemfile.lock in the same
  commit as version.rb
- set include-component-in-tag: false so tags stay vX.Y.Z and the release
  PR title stays 'chore(main): release X.Y.Z'
- add package-lock.json ($.version and $.packages[""].version) to
  extra-files so the npm lockfile version moves in the same commit too,
  making the shared relock job a no-op backstop instead of a second push

Fixes the deterministic release-PR failure + re-push/cancel churn described
in bamr87/bamr87#25.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: fix(author): build avatar path with relative_url, never protocol-relative (#306)
body:
* fix(author): build avatar path with relative_url, never protocol-relative

The avatar resolver concatenated site.baseurl + '/' + site.public_folder
+ avatar by hand. On consumer sites where public_folder is unset (remote
theme consumers do not inherit the theme _config.yml) and baseurl is
empty, a site-absolute avatar like /assets/images/logo.svg rendered as
src="//assets/images/logo.svg" — a protocol-relative URL the browser
resolves against a host named 'assets', breaking the image on every
author byline and author card.

Build the path as /<public_folder><avatar>, collapse any doubled slash,
and pass it through relative_url so baseurl handling is correct and the
output can never start with //. Full URLs (://) and the GitHub-handle
fallback are untouched, and paths under public_folder resolve exactly
as before.

Fixes #297

author: Amr
subject: fix(navigation): mark only the current page active in the sidebar nav-tree (#331)
body:
* fix(navigation): mark only the current page active in the sidebar nav-tree

`nav-tree.html` computed the active state with
`{% assign is_active = page.url == item.url %}`, but Liquid's `assign` does not
evaluate `==` — it simply stored `page.url` (a non-empty, truthy string). Every
sidebar link therefore rendered with the `.active` highlight, so a reader could
not tell which page they were on (most visible on deep nav trees).

Replace the three broken assigns (`is_active`, `child_active`, `gc_active`) with
proper conditional assigns:

    {% assign is_active = false %}{% if page.url == item.url %}{% assign is_active = true %}{% endif %}

Verified with a build: a page with a curated _data/navigation tree now renders
exactly one `.active` link (the current page) instead of one per item.

subject: feat(theme): consumer-adoption hardening — mobile overlay fixes, zero-data resilience, extension hooks (#338)
body:
* fix(sass): stop the body background from trapping mobile overlays

.zer0-bg-body force-elevated every direct child (position: relative;
z-index: 1, specificity 0,5,0), which made <main> a stacking context and
produced three consumer-reported mobile bugs: the docs-sidebar offcanvas
opened BELOW the fixed header with its close button unreachable, FABs
lost their position: fixed to the higher-specificity rule (16px of
horizontal scroll on content pages), and every overlay needed a bespoke
carve-out or id-selector escape.

The body now isolates its own stacking context and the noise overlay
paints in the negative layer (::after z-index: -1), so in-flow content
naturally sits above the texture with no per-child elevation at all.

Companion fixes:
- Lift the fixed header above Bootstrap's body-level offcanvas backdrop
  (z-index 1040) only while #bdNavbar is opening/open/closing, so the
  mobile main-nav menu paints above the dim layer and is tappable.
- auto-hide-nav.js publishes the measured header height as
  --zer0-header-height on :root so stylesheets can align overlays with
  the real header instead of hard-coding 62px.
